To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a permissionless blockchain should not be used in any of the analyzed application scenarios and that a permissioned blockchain is a suitable technical solution for Supply Chain Management and Decentralized Organizations but is not suitable for interbank and international payments.
a blockchain can be a suitable solution in scenarios in which a trusted third party is not present or in which a central database is not feasible.

1) Permissionless blockchains are not suitable to be used as a technical solution for any use case, 2) Permissioned blockchains can be used in a number of use cases, but are only superior to a centrally managed database in a few specific cases, and 3) Permissionless blockchins have no advantage over permissioned blockchains.

the question whether a blockchain is a suitable technical solution to solve the problems of the application scenarios considered in this paper.
the following research questions: (1) What are the properties of a blockchain? (2) How do these properties compare to those of a centralized database?
identifying the use cases where a blockchain is indeed a superior technical solution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a blockchain is not the right solution for every application problem.
a blockchain is not the right technical solution for every application scenario.
blockchains are not the silver bullet for all problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
blockchains are not a silver bullet and that they should only be used if the benefits outweigh the costs.
the blockchain is not a panacea, but that it can be a valuable addition in a number of application areas.

blockchains are a suitable technical solution for applications which require a decentralized and distributed ledger, which is not controlled by a single entity, which is immutable and which allows to provide a high degree of process transparency.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a blockchain is only the appropriate technical solution if the application scenario has a high need for integrity and process transparency, if there is a high number of mutually mistrusting entities involved and if the application scenario does not have a high performance requirement.
blockchains are not a silver bullet and that their applicability is limited.
the blockchain hype has to be critically questioned and the appropriate solution has to be chosen based on the application scenario and the properties of the underlying technology.
